term.readiness.full: How ready your body is today
term.readiness.line: How ready your body is for effort today, from HRV, resting heart rate and sleep.
term.readiness.body: Readiness compares last night's HRV, resting heart rate and sleep with your own earlier nights. Above your usual means your body has recovered well. It appears once OpenHoop has seen a few of your nights.
term.hrv.line: How much the time between heartbeats varies. Above your usual means rested.
term.hrv.higher:
A long night
A rest day
A calm evening
term.hrv.lower:
Alcohol
A late, heavy meal
Illness or a hard session
term.restingHr.line: Your lowest steady heart rate while asleep. Below your usual means rested.
term.restingHr.lower:
Good sleep
Steady training
A cool bedroom
term.respiratoryRate.line: Breaths per minute while you sleep. It stays steady for most people night to night.
term.respiratoryRate.higher:
Illness or fever
Alcohol
A warm room
term.spo2.line: Blood oxygen while you sleep. It normally stays high and steady.
term.spo2.lower:
High altitude
A blocked nose
A loose strap
term.skinTemp.line: Your skin temperature at the wrist while you sleep. The change matters more than the number.
term.skinTemp.cooler:
A cold room
A loose strap
term.skinTempChange.line: How much warmer or cooler your skin was than on your usual nights.
term.skinTempChange.body: How much warmer or cooler your skin was than on your usual nights. The change matters more than the number itself.
term.normalRange.name: Your normal ranges
term.normalRange.full: Where your own values usually fall
term.normalRange.line: The range your own values usually fall in, worked out from your earlier nights.
term.normalRange.body: Your normal range is where your own values usually fall: the average of your earlier nights, plus or minus the usual spread. It is not a medical reference range.
term.sleepScore.full: How well you slept against your need
term.sleepScore.line: How much of the sleep you needed you got, and how regular your times were.
term.sleepScore.body: Sleep score looks at how much of the sleep you needed you actually got, and how regular your bed and wake times were.
term.asleep.line: Time you were actually asleep, without the moments you lay awake.
term.asleep.body: The time the band saw you asleep during your main night, without the moments you lay awake.
term.asleep.method: OpenHoop finds your sleep from the band's heart rate and movement.
term.inBed.full: From falling asleep to getting up
term.inBed.line: Time from falling asleep to getting up, awake moments included.
term.inBed.body: The time from falling asleep to getting up, including the short awake moments in between.
term.sleepNeed.line: How long to sleep tonight, with extra after short nights and hard days.
term.sleepNeed.body: Your basic need, plus extra after short nights and hard days, minus naps. Getting close to it most nights keeps sleep debt low.
term.sleepDebt.line: Sleep you are short from recent nights.
term.sleepDebt.body: Sleep you missed on recent nights against your need. It adds to tonight's need until you catch up.
term.hoursVsNeed.full: Sleep you got against your need
term.hoursVsNeed.line: The hours you slept as a share of the hours you needed.
term.hoursVsNeed.body: The hours you slept as a share of the hours you needed. 100% means you got all the sleep you needed.
term.consistency.line: How close your bed and wake times are from night to night.
term.consistency.body: Going to bed and getting up at similar times helps you sleep better, even when the hours stay the same.
term.efficiency.line: The share of your time in bed that you were asleep.
term.efficiency.body: The share of your time in bed that you were asleep. When the night has sleep stages, the awake time comes from the stages.
term.stages.name: Sleep stages
term.stages.line: Light, deep and REM sleep, estimated from your heart rate and movement.
term.stages.body: Your night split into light, deep and REM sleep and awake moments. OpenHoop estimates them from your heart rate and movement, so treat them as a rough picture.
term.load.line: How hard your heart worked today, from 0 to 21. Each step up is harder to reach.
term.load.body: Load adds up how hard your heart worked today, on a scale of 0 to 21. A number from only part of a day would look too low.
term.zones.name: Heart rate zones
term.zones.line: Five bands from easy (1) to all-out (5), set by your resting and maximum heart rate.
term.zones.body: Five bands from easy (1) to all-out (5). OpenHoop sets them from your resting and maximum heart rate, so they move with your fitness.
term.stress.line: How far your heart rate and HRV drift from your calm level while you are awake and still.
term.stress.body: Stress compares your heart rate and HRV with your own calm level, only while you are awake and still. It needs a few calm days first to learn that level.
term.calories.line: Energy you burned today, estimated from your heart rate and body profile.
term.calories.body: Calories are estimated from your heart rate and your weight, height, sex and age. Without a full profile there is no estimate.
term.steps.body: Steps counted by the band's motion sensor. If you link Health Connect, its count can be shown instead.
term.wearTime.full: Time the band was on your wrist
term.wearTime.line: How long the band was on your wrist today.
term.wearTime.body: How long the band says it was on your wrist today. Numbers like HRV and Load need the band on.
explain.method.calibrated: OpenHoop's calibrated model. A wellness number, not a medical one.
explain.method.own: OpenHoop's own method. An estimate, not a diagnosis.
explain.method.range: OpenHoop works this out from your own recent nights.
why.a11y: Why there is no number yet
why.band.day: Synced {time}. The band sent heart rate for this day.
why.band.staleBody: Sync the band to bring in your latest nights.
why.nights.title: It needs more nights
why.days.title: It needs more calm days
why.need.readiness: It compares last night with your own earlier nights, so it needs {need} nights. You have {have}.
why.need.consistency: It compares your bed and wake times over {need} nights. You have {have}.
why.need.normalRange: Your usual range comes from your earlier nights, so it needs {need} nights. You have {have}.
why.need.skinTempChange: The change is measured against your usual, so it needs {need} nights. You have {have}.
why.need.stress: It learns your calm level from {need} days with enough calm, awake time. You have {have}.
why.need.generic: It compares you with your own earlier nights, so it needs a few more first.
why.expected.tonight: If you wear the band tonight.
why.expected.tonightTomorrow: If you wear the band tonight and tomorrow night.
why.expected.next: If you wear the band the next {count} nights.
why.expected.calmDays: If you have some calm, awake time each day.
why.load.title: Too little heart rate that day
why.load.body: Load needs {hours} hours of heart rate in a day. This day had {worn}.
why.load.bodyUnknown: Load needs {hours} hours of heart rate in a day. This day had less.
why.noData.nightTitle: No band data for the night
why.noData.nightBody: The band sent no sleep for this night.
why.noData.dayTitle: No band data for the day
why.noData.dayBody: The band sent no heart rate for this day.
why.source.title: Nothing to work it out from
why.source.night: It comes from your heartbeat while you sleep.
why.source.day: It comes from your heart rate during the day.
why.next.tonightBody: Wear the band to bed and sync in the morning.
why.next.todayBody: Keep the band on during the day.
why.thin.title: The signal was too noisy
why.thin.body: There was too little clean beat data from your sleep to work this out.
why.thin.fit: A snug strap, a finger's width above the wrist bone, gives cleaner readings.
why.profile.title: Your profile is missing something
why.signal.title: The band did not send this signal
why.signal.body: Without it OpenHoop cannot work this out. It can come back after the next sync.
why.footer.noGuessNight: OpenHoop never fills a gap with a guess. A night without data stays empty in your trends.
why.footer.noGuessDay: OpenHoop never fills a gap with a guess. A day without data stays empty in your trends.
